title: Live Stream Pause State

user_story.role: community member watching a live stream
user_story.value: step away and always rejoin at what is happening live

invest_check._note: Independent = false: depends on UC1's pause button/overlay mechanism — SEQUENCE after UC1 (not merge).

prioritization._note: Hardest unit to test. If PM promotes to Must, it enlarges the critical path. Workaround if deferred: today's resume-from-pause is degraded-but-functional.

preconditions: User is watching a live stream with Room status: live
entry_points: A. User deliberately pauses the live stream via the central pause button (per UC1)

platforms._boundary: mobile web CANNOT pause a Live stream (BR-02) — excluded from pause/resume scope (AC-05).

business_rules.statement: Seek/skip (±10s) controls exist only on video/recorded — never on active Live.
Pause/resume of an active Live stream is not available on mobile web (offered on iOS, Android, web-desktop only).
The pause indicator IS the central play (▶) button overlay itself — not a separate badge or banner.
First-tap interaction model is platform-dependent (mobile reveal / desktop 1-step).
Play/pause changes only via explicit user pause/play (BR-09) or a terminal room state (BR-12) — no implicit op (incl. a network stall) toggles it.
Paused overlay persists and dismisses only on a tap outside the play button; the stream stays paused.
A terminal room state (ended/recorded) always takes priority over the paused state; resolves to ended regardless of recording-processing readiness (no 'processing' state).
Resume target by media type: video/recorded → exact paused position; Live → current live edge within normal buffering tolerance (a few seconds behind live is expected).
Live chat is independent of playback state — keeps running during pause, never replayed/skipped on resume.
The viewer is never left on a frozen frame with no feedback — interruptions surface an explicit state (Reconnecting w/ auto-retry, or ended).

acceptance_criteria.scenario: Pause live → pause indicator (▶) + chat stays live + tap-outside dismisses (no seek)
given: the user is watching a live stream at the live edge (Room status = live)
(mobile) the controls overlay is revealed per UC1  /  (desktop) direct-tap pause is available
acceptance_criteria.when: the user pauses via the central pause button
then: the central play (▶) button overlay is shown as the pause indicator (LS-mobile-04; no separate badge)
the chat continues to receive and display new messages in real time — it is not paused
the LIVE badge / viewer-count stays as-is (updating it is out of scope — a separate enhancement)
tapping anywhere outside the play button dismisses the overlay control (pause/play button only — a Live stream has no seek controls) — the stream remains paused

acceptance_criteria.scenario: Resume → current live moment (not paused position); chat uninterrupted
given: the user has paused a live stream (chat kept running live during the pause)
acceptance_criteria.when: the user resumes (the stream restarts) via the play button
then: playback starts from the current live moment — not from the previous paused position
the pause indicator (▶ overlay) dismisses
the chat remains uninterrupted — no messages are missed or replayed
acceptance_criteria._test_tolerance: resume lands within normal live buffering tolerance — a few seconds behind live is EXPECTED (CONF-07). Assert '≈ live within tolerance', NOT exact-live. This is a behaviour CHANGE vs today's resume-from-pause → test the NEW behaviour on every platform.

clarifications_needed.question: Is the 'a few seconds behind live' buffering tolerance acceptable to product as the resume target? (Tighter is not achievable — live-streaming physics.)

acceptance_criteria.scenario: Stream ends while paused → ended/recorded wins, no frozen frame
given: the user has paused a live stream
acceptance_criteria.when: the Room transitions to ended or recorded during the pause
then: the player moves to an appropriate ended or recorded state
the ended/recorded state always takes priority over the paused state (even if both occur simultaneously)
the viewer is not left on a frozen frame with no feedback
if the recording is not yet ready, the player shows 'Livestream ended' — there is no intermediate 'processing' state

acceptance_criteria.scenario: Default — playing at live edge, before any pause
given: a live stream (Room status = live) is playing at the live edge
acceptance_criteria.when: the viewer has not yet paused
then: no pause indicator is shown
the chat is live
the LIVE badge / viewer count displays as-is (unaffected by this feature)

acceptance_criteria.scenario: Default — mobile web has no pause control on Live
given: a viewer is on mobile web watching a 'Live' stream
then: no pause control is offered — pause/resume of a Live stream is not available on web-mobile
acceptance_criteria._note: Standing platform boundary (platform table 68264), not a bug. Exclude web-mobile from UC2 pause/resume test scope.

acceptance_criteria.scenario: Long pause → resume lands further behind live, still within tolerance
given: the user paused a live stream for an extended period (minutes)
then: playback snaps to the current live moment (per AC-02) — the size of the jump does not change the guarantee
a brief buffering/loading state is acceptable while the jump completes

acceptance_criteria.scenario: Chat/video re-sync on resume — no replayed/skipped messages
given: the user paused for a while (chat kept running live throughout)
acceptance_criteria.when: the user resumes (video snaps to the current live moment)
then: chat and video are aligned at the live moment — no chat messages are replayed or skipped
the transition is smooth; brief buffering is acceptable

acceptance_criteria.scenario: Network drops while paused → Reconnecting, stays paused, resume→live
given: the user has paused a live stream
acceptance_criteria.when: the network connection drops and later recovers
then: a 'Reconnecting' indicator is shown (auto-retry, no manual button) — the viewer is not left on a no-feedback frozen frame
the stream stays paused through the drop→recover cycle — no auto-resume
on user resume, playback snaps to the current live moment / live edge (per AC-02)
acceptance_criteria._resolved_by_code: iOS: reconnecting overlay tied to device network — shows even while paused; resume → seekToLiveEdge()+play() (LiveStreamViewerView.swift:244-272, LiveStreamPlayerView.swift:27-50). Web: 'Reconnecting' overlay on playback stall + HLS.js auto-retry — generally NOT shown while paused. See platform-behavior-notes.md.
